Rape

Toolbox feat. Ani
2. Robyn Tatu (USA) -- 2 GW 9 VP -- 0 VP -- Lasombra Mid Cap Bleed w/
Black Hand Tech
2. Ruben Feldmann (SUI) -- 2 GW 9 VP -- 0 VP -- Pander Vote

Last Chance Qualifier: October 3rd, 2009
1. Ferenc Vasadi (HUN) -- 3 GW 8 VP -- 3 VP -- Ravnos Wall feat.
Gabrin
2. Bill Troxel (USA) -- 2 GW 9 VP -- 2 VP -- !Malk/Malk Dive into
Madness Bleed
2. Erol Ongun (GER) -- 1 GW 6.5 VP -- 0 VP -- Stanislava & Friends
Vote & Bloat
2. Nick Miller (AUS) -- 1 GW 5 VP -- 0 VP -- Ravnos Stealth Bleed
2. Michael Heyder (GER) -- 1 GW 4.5 VP -- 0 VP -- Guruhi Bruise &
Bleed

When you look at the three major events (LCQ, Day 1, Day 2) that two
players, Michael and Ferenc did appear in all three finals. While
Michael stuck to his successful Guruhi deck, Ferenc switched his deck
three times.

The metagame on the LCQ was very diversified, since the already
qualified players tried often something more quirky decks. The
metagame on Day 1 was totally aggressive. Grab a GW, and get qualified
at any cost. Allegedly there was one table with the following five
decks: three KS S&B decks, one Obfuscate&Presence deck and one Nergal
Turbo deck. The metagame on Day 2 was completely different; the S&B
faction was almost not present, and mostly big cap vote and wall decks
were played.

In any case a great experience for all participants, and I want to
thank you the participants for attending, LSJ for judging the
tournaments and the organizers for the tournament David & Robyn Tatu,
Jeff Thompson and Oscar Garza for their huge efforts for making the
tournament happen. Thank you very much.

Best Regards, Ralf

Messages.Author: Matthew T. Morgan
Messages.Body:
Not such a good showing for team USA this year. The Euros swept all the
main tournaments and Americans only had one seat at each of the LCQ, day 1
and day 2 tournaments. In fact, I was the only American to score a game
win on day 2. I tried to confuse the issue by insisting that Michael was
in fact the American and therefore should be ousted first, but for some
reason that didn't work. I really think that was my strongest strategy
and best opportunity to win, but maybe one of the observers can point out
where I went wrong.

The only solution I can think of to this problem is to start claiming
Ruben for Team USA, since he lives in New York now.

At 3rd seed, I had the choice to prey on Michael (Guruhi block/combat) or
Hugh (!Ventrue block/bleed/some combat). Since I knew Hugh's deck didn't
rush and didn't come forward too quickly (at least not without an
irresponsible bleeder behind it), I chose to prey on Michael, figuring he
wouldn't rush me out of existence right away, giving a VP to someone else.
I was right about that at least. Ferenc chose to sit as Hugh's prey, then
Ruben chose to sit as Ferenc's prey. Michael went first.

Michael had a horrible crypt draw, but unfortunately for me, Ruben came at
me so fast, I had no opportunity to capitalize on Michael's bad luck.
Ruben played The Parthenon and Zillah's Valley, getting Selma on turn 1.
I put four on Anson. On turn 2, Ruben played Legendary Vampire on Selma,
then played Kaymakli Nightmares, which gave me basically the same crypt
draw, but meant I wouldn't get Anson until turn 3. It also improved
Michael's draw. Luckily, Ferenc had played a Dreams and already had Baron
Dieudonne in play. Ruben hit me for 8 again (Parity Shift/bleed) on turn
3, so I had just 6 pool remaining when I put Anson into play.

Team not-Ruben (me, Ferenc and Hugh, who had a vote from Joseph O'Grady
and didn't want Ruben to run the table so quickly) managed to vote away
the Legendary Vampire and Ferenc gave me 3 pool by shifting Ruben. I
survived another turn as Ruben got out Suhailia and another Legendary
Vampire. I Minion Tapped Anson and avoided the 4 bleed from Suhailia by
tapping her with Scalpel Tongue before she could bleed me when Selma
called a vote. Ferenc asked me if I would help him kill Ruben. There was
obviously some discussion, but I agreed to help and in exchange, he
wouldn't come forward until I had a 2nd vampire, so Ruben was out first.
I had 11 pool left.

Meanwhile, Michael was tooling up undisturbed and had a Fame on Hugh's
Neighbor John. Hugh was attempting to conserve fortitude cards and still
make some headway against Ferenc. Nothing much happened for a few turns
other than Hugh's Owain feeding Anson blood, so I could Minion Tap again
(costing 3 due to Villain!). I put Alexandra into play in an attempt to
have some kind of game. By now Michael had three Guruhi out, including
Nanglia Were. He had some Raven Spies and stuff and quite a lot of pool.
It looked glum. I was hoping he might get overconfident and go too low
and I could kill him with a TGB vote, but those odds were slim. Ruben had
taken Anthelios with him when he died, so there was no recycling for me.

Ferenc eventually Parity Shifted some of my pool to him and bled me kind
of low with Petrodon. Hugh saw his time was up as Michael was very close
to killing him, so he tapped out Ferenc and Pentexed one of his guys and
went for the lunge. Ferenc had sufficient wakes and survived. He also
AI'd Owain on a bleed for 6. Very bad for Team Not Gonna Get VPs.
Ferenc hit me again after removing the Pentex and I was almost dead.
Michael was at 13 pool with one untapped vampire. I had two Aires and a
KRC. If Michael had zero wakes (fat chance, as he had hardly played any),
I could kill him. Any chance is better than no chance, so I played my own
Pentex and called the KRC. Michael blocked, so I resigned myself to
death. Hugh and I both died around the same time.

Once strong, Ferenc was much weaker than Michael now. Michael had a ton
of pool and four minions, including a rusher. There wasn't much doubt how
things would come out at that point.

Fun game. I look forward to some rematches in Palma. Hopefully I will
have a better deck. Mine is okay, but it's a bit slow and a lot can go
wrong. This is the first tournament in which Villeins really hurt me. I
could've played Villeins myself, but they aren't recycleable with
Anthelios, since they stay in play. That's why I played Minion Taps.
My deck wasn't really a big Parity Shift deck. It only has two in sixty
cards. The six Ashur Tables I played weren't a huge help in three of my
games, but they were somewhat instrumental in the 3rd round which I won.
The Ambulance angle was never useful, which is too bad, because it's a fun
trick, but I was never able to put more than one Aching Beauty into play,
so it wasn't that huge. It would probably be better as just a plain TGB
deck with or without the Ashur Tablets or as an Aching Beauty deck that
has more defense.

Anyway, I had a great time and wish I could've come for the full week.
Thanks to all the organizers and congratulations to the winners,
especially our champion, Michael "The American" Heyder!

Matt Morgan

I've got plenty, but by the first round of responses, its clear that
Jyhad old-timers don't see a particular problem... None of the
discussion that might follow is particularly worthwhile, if we're
still in the "denial" phase.

If the consensus is to stay in Google Groups, at least move it out of
Usenet, and into Google Groups proper, and ditch "Jyhad", which is
hasn't been named for over a decade...

Search "VTES" from the top search window at groups.google.com;

http://groups.google.com/groups/dir?lnk=nhpsfg&q=VTES&qt_s=Search+for+a+group

Results

1. VTES in Vilnius (22 members)

2. VTES in LA (47 members)

3, VTES Northen Minnesota (22 members)

4. Domain Canberra (47 members)

etc

Usenet groups don't even show up in Google Groups search results.
Assuming a gamer has interest in VTES, they're not going to find the
main discussion forum without some serious assistance...

Oh, and to Peter; I wasn't discussing the NAC turnout, specifically,
which is clearly been affected by the economic downturn... but rather
the impact that minimal visibility has on US interest in the game.
While I don't play much at all any more, I do keep tabs on the gaming
industry through a bunch of mainstream channels; industry ones like
icv2, GAMA, etc and social network sites (facebook, etc.) I don't see
VTES visible on them to any signfiicant degree. If I wasn't already
aware of the game, I wouldn't know it exists. The hidden/buried
player discussion forum was probably just the first example of "lack
of visibility" that came to my mind.

Getting off the topic of player visibility, and into wider game
visibility, A WW free play game promoting VTES (or even V:tR) on
facebook/myspace ala "DnD Tiny Adventures" with the "Paypal for perks"
option would be an excellent promotional tool. I have no clue why WW
is letting Zynga et. al. get whatever revenue is out there from games
like Vampire Wars, when they're the ones who practically re-invented
vampires as a modern gaming genre. In that respect, WW's own lack of
corporate visibility is part and parcel of VTES's problem... its not
just the players and where they talk, although given VTES's
"grassroots" nature, that plays a not insignficant role, IMO.

Haven't heard it mentioned yet, but why not move the NAC to Origins?

White-Wolf already supports VTES there. Is buying more table space to
support an NAC at Origins that much more than the cost of hosting it
later in the year at a separate location?

Spend a little extra in advertising the events. All the other games
had banners/cardboard displays that advertised what game was played in
that section. Get a nice banner to hang on the wall or some such.
Personally, I'd be more inclined to go check out a game advertising a
North American Championship than one that's only unique feature is a
laptop older than half the attendees at Origins. Strategic use of the
nice VTES table cloths and stealing one of the loud people's round
tables for the finals. Set it up and only use it for any finals game.

You have the extra bonus of Origins being there. I'll wager most
V:TES players also have some interest in other gaming related events
held there too. It is much easier to justify to yourself the cost of
attending an NAC if you're also attending a major convention at the
same time.

The US Nationals could be moved back to GenCon, or even kept at
Origins as a predecessor tournament.

Wed US Nats + miniQ, Thu miniQ + LCQ. Fri Day 1 NAC + draft/Rapid
Thought after. Sat Day 2 NAC. Sun First Chance Qualifier.

NAC and EC are 4-6 months apart then.

Downsides:
First year causes issues with qualified players. Solution is to carry
over all players from the previous year once to make up for only
having half a year to qualify.

Combines two big draw events for VTES into one. Origins has a
generally loyal following of attendees. The NAC itself will generally
see a good showing itself for being the NAC.

Week of Nightmares events leading up to it don't fit into the Origins
schedule. Maybe having them hosted locally in Columbus could work,
but having to get hotels before and during Origins may cause some
issues. Maybe scrap the traditional leadup, or even run 3-4 events a
day leading up to the major tourneys.

Just some thoughts. Not expecting it to have a chance in hell of
happening, but putting a solution out there.

Or perhaps he just believes that the correct way to handle posts clearly
outside the bounds of the agreed-upon topic for the forum is to inform
the transgressors, as opposed to simply muzzling them (and maybe informing
them as well, depending on the behavior of the particular moderator). The
former has a few distinct advantages over the latter:

1) You can be sure the transgressor has been informed of his error. In a
moderated system, you can't be.

2) Besides informing the transgressor, other prospective transgressors also
have a chance to see the objection in advance. The issue gets some short-
term visibility which can be beneficial (although such posts also qualify
as more short-term noise WRT the discussion topic, it has to be granted).

3) Net.cops who are out of line with the true meaning of the discussion
topic agreement (formalized in Usenet as the newsgroup charter) are
corrected by other net.cops. This is useful whether the mistake was
accidental or deliberate. Moderators, on the other hand, have no check.
In fact, it may not be possible to even see when they're (mis)using their
power, depending on how the mechanism of moderation works.

4) Although personality conflicts are more likely to arise, they're less
likely to be too severe (at least in a good, congenial newsgroup).

Fred
